candidate.title: A Safe Two-Scheme Key Cycle for Every Encryption Scheme
candidate.informal: Key cycles are not safe to publish in general. But the counterexamples build a pair of schemes that break each other, and this conjecture asks the opposite question: given any public-key encryption scheme, can one always find a partner scheme such that the two-step cycle across the two schemes is safe to publish?
candidate.formal_statement_latex: For every valid, IND-CPA secure public key encryption scheme $\mathsf{E}$ there exist a valid encryption scheme $\mathsf{E}'$ and injective key encodings $\psi, \psi'$ such that the scheme obtained from $\mathsf{E}$ by appending $\mathsf{Enc}^{*}(pk, \psi'(sk'))$ and $(\mathsf{Enc}')^{*}(pk', \psi(sk))$ to the public key, for an independently generated $(sk', pk') \gets \mathsf{Gen}'(\kappa)$, is IND-CPA secure.
candidate.printed_statement: Conjecture 2: For any (public key) encryption scheme Enc there is a (possibly different) encryption scheme Enc' such that Enc(pk, .) is secure in the presence of side information Enc'_{pk'}(sk), Enc_{pk}(sk') for a randomly chosen key pair (pk', sk').
candidate.status_note: Printed as `Conjecture 2' in the source's concluding Section 6 (p. 20), immediately after the sentence saying that the known separation results do not rule it out. Open in both directions.
candidate.risks: As literally printed the conjecture is trivially true, because the source's Definition 1 does not require an `encryption scheme' to be correct: a scheme whose ciphertexts are independent of the message satisfies it vacuously. The draft's Remark 1 says so and requires validity. Also, the printed statement puts no security hypothesis on Enc, without which the conclusion fails trivially; the draft adds IND-CPA security of Enc and flags the addition.

However, this is different from computing a simple cycle Encpk (sk) directly, because the evaluated ciphertext follows a different distribution. So, it is not ruled out by previous separation results, and we conjecture the following.
However, for the purpose of applying (a generalization of) Theorem 6 it is not necessary to use the same encryption scheme at every step of the cycle.
Note that the new (existentially quantified) scheme Enc′ is not required to be homomorphic.
Still, proving that the conjecture is true would provide interesting information about the feasibility of achieving circular security in a generic way.

Previous results have shown how to build encryption schemes Enc such that publishing such a cycle is insecure. So, one cannot achieve full composability generically by publishing such an encryption cycle for any scheme Enc.

verify.reason: The conjecture is printed verbatim and left open, and the source explains precisely why the existing separations do not apply. Two gaps in the printed statement had to be closed to make it non-vacuous -- validity of the partner scheme and IND-CPA security of the starting scheme -- and both are recorded as the draft's own additions rather than presented as the source's.

checks.name: existence
checks.finding: Printed as a displayed, labelled conjecture.

checks.name: openness
checks.finding: Posed in the last section; the following paragraph discusses variants and consequences but settles nothing. Nothing after p. 20 but references.

checks.name: strength
checks.finding: Stated at the source's strength: the 2-cycle public-key form only. The source's listed variants (longer cycles, private-key Enc', bitwise encryption) are named in the draft's setting and explicitly excluded from the statement.

checks.name: quantifiers
checks.finding: The for-all/exists shape is the point of the conjecture and is preserved. Two implicit hypotheses were made explicit: validity of Enc' and IND-CPA security of Enc. Without the first the statement is vacuous, see the draft's Remark 1.

checks.name: attribution
checks.finding: The paper's own conjecture. The separations it says do not apply are attributed in the draft to KRW15, KW16, AP16, GKW17a, GKW17b, HK17, exactly the keys the source cites at that point.

checks.name: definitions
checks.finding: Encryption scheme, validity and IND-CPA are the source's Definitions 1 and 2. The key encodings psi, psi' are named by the draft because the source writes Enc'_{pk'}(sk) with the encoding implicit; that is a renaming, not a redefinition.

checks.name: fabrication
checks.finding: The claims about what a proof would and would not give are quoted from the source's own paragraph, including the caveat that the conjecture does not by itself imply composable FHE.

checks.name: self-containment
checks.finding: Definitions 1-3 plus Conjecture 2 of the draft are enough to know what to prove.

corrections.problem: A degenerate Enc' whose ciphertexts do not depend on the message satisfies the printed statement without forming a cycle at all.
corrections.corrected: Require Enc' to be valid, i.e. perfectly correct, and say in a remark that the source leaves this implicit.

corrections.problem: The printed statement quantifies over any encryption scheme Enc, including insecure ones, for which the conclusion is false.
corrections.corrected: Restrict to IND-CPA secure Enc and flag the restriction.
